best_for: People on Windows or a Mac who open and edit SQLite files by hand, including encrypted ones, and who want either the current Letos release or an installer from the older SQLiteStudio 3.4 line.
description:
Letos is a desktop editor for SQLite databases from letos.org, the project formerly known as SQLiteStudio. You can create, browse and edit databases in one window, with panels you can move and dock where you want them.

The SQL editor shows syntax hints, marks errors and formats your code, and a Ctrl+click on a table name in a query opens that table. A single query can reach several databases at once. You can draw an entity relationship diagram, or build one from an existing database and apply changes back to it. Drag tables and indexes from one database to another to copy or move them. A History tab keeps past queries, and Letos can fill tables with sample data for testing.

points.title: SQLiteStudio is now called Letos
points.text: The project took the name Letos to avoid confusion with the official SQLite project, starting with 4.0.0 in June 2026. This page keeps both: Letos 4.0.0 to 4.0.4 under the winget ID `PawelSalawa.Letos`, and SQLiteStudio 3.4.1 to 3.4.21 under the old ID `PawelSalawa.SQLiteStudio`.

points.title: Free, with no paid edition
points.text: It is GPL-3.0 software that the project describes as free for any purpose, commercial use included. There is no paid edition and no telemetry, and donations are optional.

points.title: Opens encrypted SQLite variants
points.text: Besides plain SQLite files, it handles password-protected databases made with SQLCipher, WxSQLite3 and System.Data.SQLite. Installing registers it for extensions such as .db, .db3, .sqlite and .sqlite3.

points.title: Scripted functions in JavaScript, Python or Tcl
points.text: You can write your own scalar and aggregate SQL functions, collations and data generators in JavaScript, Python or Tcl. Plugins can add further scripting languages, import and export formats and database formats.

points.title: Import and export options
points.text: Import takes CSV, or any text file parsed with a regular expression. Export writes SQL statements, CSV, HTML, XML, PDF and JSON.

points.title: Letos on Windows: x64 and Arm64, per user or machine-wide
points.text: Letos 4 has Inno Setup installers for x64 and Arm64, with no 32-bit build. Each one installs for the current user with `/CURRENTUSER` or for the whole machine with `/ALLUSERS`. Zip builds that run without installing are on the release page but not listed here.

points.title: SQLiteStudio 3.4 installers run unattended
points.text: The 3.4 releases come as x86 and x64 .exe installers that install for the whole machine. They run silently with `--mode unattended --unattendedmodeui none`, take `--install_for all` for every user and `--prefix` for a custom folder. They are the last builds with a 32-bit Windows option.

points.title: Mac gets Letos only, and needs macOS 13
points.text: The Mac download here is the universal DMG for Intel and Apple silicon, from the Homebrew cask, which asks for macOS 13 or later. Letos also publishes a separate macos11 DMG for older Macs, and Linux AppImage and tar.xz builds for x64 and Arm64, none of which are listed here. Only the current Mac release is kept.
